text: The paper’s central contribution is an extensive empirical study yielding design guidelines for personalized LLM deployment on resource-constrained edge devices, jointly varying model choice, customization method (multiple PEFT methods vs. RAG), compression, data scale, and training time. Closest prior work is scattered across narrower studies: Li et al. (2024) and Liu et al. (2024) analyze quantization and architectural choices for on-device models; Pu et al. (2023) and Ding et al. (2023) benchmark PEFT/LoRA trade-offs and convergence; Zhang et al. (2024) studies scaling laws for finetuning methods; and Qin et al. (2023) explores on-device personalization with fixed LoRA settings. These works each cover portions of the design space (e.g., PEFT vs. full tuning, quantization impact, LoRA behavior) but do not jointly consider personalization methods, compression schemes, hyperparameter sweeps, and explicit device-level constraints in a unified framework, nor do they contrast LoRA with RAG or derive time-budgeted training recommendations for edge hardware. The submission’s added value is thus a broader, more integrated empirical mapping and concrete edge-specific heuristics (e.g., LoRA rank/alpha defaults, LoRA vs. RAG by task difficulty, 3–4 hour training sufficiency). Given that this central, integrative empirical contribution is not directly challenged, the paper constitutes a genuine advance in novelty.
